title: Abba bar Chanana
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Also called Chinana or Chanina. He appears in Jerusalem Talmud Eruvin 8:4 and at the beginning of Gittin, chapter 3, after Rav and Rav Assi and before Rabbi Yohanan and Resh Lakish. Bereshit Rabbah 63:7 has Rabbi Levi reporting him. Berakhot 30a, according to Dikdukei Soferim, reads Rav Abba bar Chanina; our text reads Rav Huna bar Chiyya. After examination, Hyman considers it apparent that he was Rabbi Chanina bar Chama’s son. Midrash Shmuel, chapter 13, has Rabbi Chanina saying: “When I ascended from the exile, I loosened my belt, my animal’s, and that of Abba my son.” The source is Jerusalem Talmud Peah 7:3, but the son’s name is missing there.

notes.text: The checked Berakhot has Huna bar Chinnana, whereas Hyman supplies Huna bar Chiyya; his Dikdukei Soferim reading and father–son identification remain distinct. The son’s omitted name in Peah is Hyman’s argument.

The consulted Midrash Shmuel 13 explicitly has Rabbi Chanina’s son Abba in the belt-and-carob-tree account. The consulted Berakhot 30a instead has Huna bar Chinnana; Hyman supplies Huna bar Chiyya and reports a Dikdukei Soferim Abba reading. The father–son identification and the claimed Peah omission are Hyman’s argument, not an identity established by a shared name.
